headline: High: open-webui’s broad network/MCP and shared-session surfaces can amplify AutoGPT outputs into unsafe actions, leakage, and compliance risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and act on filesystem content and shell outputs, while open-webui exposes MCP, OpenAPI tools, and file-backed inputs. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if open-webui forwards untrusted content into AutoGPT workflows. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF open-webui forwards user-uploaded documents or tool output into AutoGPT prompts without provenance tags, injection is possible.
IF AutoGPT consumes filesystem content originating from open-webui as instructions, the pathway is active.
mitigations: Disable automatic prompting from uploaded files.
Add provenance labels to all tool and file content.
Require a human review step before AutoGPT executes instructions from open-webui.
Restrict MCP/OpenAPI tools to allowlisted, read-only endpoints.
requires-engineering: implement content-sanitization and instruction-separation guards.

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui handles API keys, documents, notes, and persistent memory, and can call broad external services; AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress. If they share a workspace or mounted volume, sensitive open-webui data can be read and exfiltrated through AutoGPT’s execution path. The pairwise leakage risk is therefore high in common deployments.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or mounted volume, open-webui documents or API keys can be exposed to AutoGPT.
IF AutoGPT is allowed to transmit retrieved file contents through its allowlisted egress, leakage can leave the host.
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different volumes.
Remove secrets from any shared directory.
Turn off file upload sharing between the two agents.
Limit AutoGPT egress to a null route or strict allowlist.
requires-engineering: add per-file access controls and secret redaction.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, and open-webui can run browsers, spawn subprocesses, and supports multiple instances with shared session state. If both are pointed at the same mutable workspace, they can overwrite files or race on shared artifacts. The profiles do not prove a lock, so the conflict is plausible and nontrivial.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or mounted volume, file races and overwrites can occur.
IF open-webui sessions share mutable state while AutoGPT edits the same artifacts, conflicts are likely.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Disable concurrent writes to shared artifacts.
Use per-agent locks around any shared file.
Run one agent at a time for the same project folder.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can present tool outputs, documents, and persistent memory to downstream workflows, while AutoGPT can generate unverified content and act via shell or subprocesses. If open-webui treats AutoGPT output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect actions or persisted bad state. Because both agents have action-capable surfaces, the blast radius is high.
conditions: IF open-webui feeds AutoGPT output into tools, memory, or documents without verification, errors propagate.
IF either agent is allowed to act on the other’s output automatically, downstream mistakes can become persistent.
mitigations: Require explicit verification before any action-taking step.
Mark AutoGPT outputs as untrusted by default.
Disable automatic writes to memory or documents from agent output.
Add a second-pass checker for factual claims.
requires-engineering: enforce typed handoffs between generation and execution.

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui explicitly handles API keys, documents, notes, and usage analytics, while AutoGPT has filesystem and shell access. If regulated or sensitive data is routed through open-webui and then exposed to AutoGPT’s local execution context, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not show matching compliance controls, so the mismatch is medium.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are placed in open-webui and shared with AutoGPT, compliance obligations may be violated.
IF retention or deletion policies differ across the shared data path, subject-rights handling can fail.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared folders.
Do not route secrets from open-webui into AutoGPT.
Document retention settings for both agents.
Restrict open-webui to non-sensitive projects.
requires-engineering: align residency, logging, and deletion controls across both systems.
